messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert -> synthetic-checks-prod / canary-eu fired (CRITICAL) - 5 consecutive failures. Probe: canary-inference-eu-01.
pagerduty-bot: Incident #INC-91234 created and routed to primary oncall.
alex_g: Acked oncall alert, jumping in. taking ownership for now.
emily: Any customer-facing latency or errors reported?
alex_g: Not seeing customer tickets yet. Metrics show probe 5xx rate ~18% and p95 latency jumped to 1.2s from baseline 120ms in eu-west-1.
raj_p: On infra side, I can see increased connection resets to gpu-infer-02 in eu cluster around the same time.
alex_g: Rolling logs from canary probe: 
```
2026-03-14T15:03:10Z probe: request failed status=502 host=gpu-infer-02 conn_err=read reset
2026-03-14T15:03:11Z probe: request failed status=502 host=gpu-infer-03 err=kv-cache-miss
2026-03-14T15:03:12Z probe: success latency=0.12s host=gpu-infer-01
```
raj_p: Looks like a partial degradation on a subset of GPU nodes, maybe kernel OOMs or network flaps. I'm going to check node metrics.
tim_s: I'm going to escalate to secondary if primary doesn't ack resumption in 3m. Also setting a 15m suppression for repeat pages for the canary so it doesn't thrash.
sara_m: @alex_g can you confirm if routing fallback is active? We have fallback model variants for canary traffic that avoid gpu-infer-02/03.
alex_g: Initiating fallback routing: updating canary policy to prefer gpu-infer-01 and software-quant path. command: `curl -XPOST https://ops.redwood/api/routing/override -d '{"probe":"canary-inference-eu-01","prefer_hosts":["gpu-infer-01"]}'`
raj_p: I scaled up canary pool by +2 instances (spin up gpu-infer-04/05) to absorb traffic and reduce tail latency.
emily: Good. Any downstream customers impacted (embeddings, search)?
alex_g: Gateway logs: only probe traffic hit failures. No spike in customer 5xx from prod gateways. Looks isolated to canary/test prefix. Marking customer impact: none at this time.
pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-91234 status -> acknowledged by alex_g.
raj_p: Found repeated kernel-level NIC resets on gpu-infer-03. I've drained it from the pool and kicked an automated reprovision.
alex_g: Restarted canary probe service on probe-host-7 (`systemctl restart canary-probe.service`) and verified initial checks green.
tim_s: I've silenced the PagerDuty rule for this check for 15m to avoid noisy re-pages while we stabilize.
emily: Thanks all — no customer impact, mitigation in place (drain + reprovision + fallback routing). Recommend we: 1) keep watch for 30m, 2) open a follow-up infra ticket to investigate NIC firmware on gpu-infer-03, 3) post a short incident note.
sara_m: Agreed. @raj_p please create infra ticket and assign to kernel team. @alex_g please add short incident note to INC-91234 with timeline.
alex_g: Will add notes now. Adding quick TL;DR: canary probe failures due to NIC resets on gpu-infer-03 -> drained & reprovisioned -> probe back to green -> no customer impact.
incident-bot: Incident INC-91234 marked RESOLVED by alex_g.
alex_g: Closing thread — monitoring for 30m then will handoff to postmortem if repeats. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
